items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: I'll leave that to Dr. Shushone and Mr. Meyer Menville to explain to me that rhythm came from Africa.

ctx.x: So now how did this trombone play as different say from Edwards?

Well, he never played any kind of trombone until years after. You'd have to verify that by the records he supposed to have played with different bands. Edwards was the daddy of all modern trombone players. And nobody could compete with Edwards on the trombone. Although he and I are enemies today. I'll give him what is due. The man was the greatest trombone player of his age. He invented many tricks on the trombone. Which was to be followed by men like Miff Moe. Tea gardens and all of them. Which they improved.…

would have to make up such stuff to fake, like brrrr through a horn. And different other little things that he didn't know the tune would add, different little things, which later became known as jazz licks or jazz idioms. It was just like a fake, a bunch of gypsies, didn't know nothing. And not knowing the tune, we'd fall back on it. Now I could tell you, many of the fellows, they put them all together these tunes, these idioms. They'll start do all together. When he finished that one chord construction with…
